messages.subject: Mamba.jl includes NUTS
parts:
I checked it out and it has user define unconstrained density
and gradient directly for NUTS.  Otherwise, the interface looks
nice.  Rob used Mamba.jl in Stan.jl for posterior analysis.

- Bob

Begin forwarded message:

From: Benjamin Deonovic <benjamin...@uiowa.edu>
Subject: Stan.jl presentation at JuliaCon 2015
Date: August 18, 2015 at 6:24:18 PM EDT
To: bob.ca...@columbia.edu

Dr. Carpenter,

I'm a student at the University of Iowa and one of the collaborators with Brian Smith on Mamba.jl.

I was watching your talk online on Stan.jl from JuliaCon and you mentioned Mamba.jl as a tool for posterior analysis and visualization of MCMC output and that other "within-Julia" competitors to Stan.jl were Lora.jl and Sigma.jl.

I just wanted to point out that Mamba.jl is a fully fleshed out (and documented!) MCMC package (much more so than Lora.jl) which implements all kinds of samplers from Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (NUTS), slice sampling, and adaptive Metropolis-Hastings.

So if you guys ever need to compare MCMC runs from Stan.jl to something in Julia feel free to check our package out!

https://github.com/brian-j-smith/Mamba.jl
http://mambajl.readthedocs.org/en/latest/ (currently getting updated to reflect an update in the internal machinery)

Benjamin
